title: Locate Inventory
real_world_story: A warehouse stores product IDs in an unsorted inventory list. When a worker needs to locate a product, the system first organizes the IDs and then searches efficiently for the requested product.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Product IDs stored in the warehouse
real_world_connection.target_represents: Product ID requested by the worker
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Sorting inventory data and efficiently locating a product

problem_statement: Given an array of product IDs and a target product ID, sort the IDs in non-decreasing order and use binary search to find the target. Return its index in the sorted array. If the target does not exist, return -1.
task: Organize the inventory and efficiently locate the requested product.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N integers representing product IDs. The third line contains an integer target representing the product ID to search for.
output_format: Print the zero-based index of the target product in the sorted array. If the product does not exist, print -1.

examples.explanation: After sorting, the product IDs are 102, 204, 301, 405, 509, 708. Product ID 509 is at index 4.
After sorting, 700 is not present in the inventory.

expected_algorithm.reason: Sorting organizes the inventory, after which binary search can locate the requested product efficiently.

hint: Use binary search on the sorted array.
Return the position of the target if it is found.
real_world_takeaway: Organizing inventory data before searching allows warehouse systems to locate products much faster.
